description:
Across the world fuel prices are hitting record highs - as the US war with Iran continues beyond its seventh month. 
 
In the UK, energy bills continue to rise - inflation in Germany has hit its highest level in almost three years - and last month the US federal reserve raised the cost of borrowing for the first time in more than three years. The crunch is real - and being felt everywhere. 
 
During this special programme presented by Maryam Moshiri we take a global perspective - with our global teams we hear about the impact - from Asia to Africa and explain what is being done, and what you as a consumer can do too.

author: BBC News
description:
A Scottish Sikh activist has been released from prison in India after being detained for almost nine years without being convicted.

Jagtar Singh Johal thanked "the almighty" as he walked free from gate three of the Tihar Prison complex in Delhi.

The 39-year-old from Dumbarton was arrested in 2017 over allegations he had a role in a series of targeted killings of religious and political figures - which he denies.

Johal was granted bail at Delhi High Court on 18 September, but has only now been released from detention.

author: BBC News
description:
Tennessee death row prisoner Christa Pike survived two attempted lethal injections on Wednesday - raising further concerns across the US about the use of the drug pentobarbital in executions, and capital punishment in general. 

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has ordered a full investigation, and temporarily halted all executions scheduled for later this year. 

The UN human rights chief Volker Turk has urged the state not to make a new attempt to execute Pike, saying the physical and mental suffering arising from failed executions is "abhorrent and cruel". 

Christa Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer.

description:
How did the passengers of Flydubai's flight FZ1073 prevent a catastrophe after a cockpit attack? And what does this incident mean for Israel at a politically charged moment? 

On Wednesday, a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to Saudi Arabia after one pilot allegedly stabbed the other. The aircraft entered a 17,000ft plunge before passengers and crew forced their way into the cockpit, overpowered the alleged attacker and helped bring the plane back under control. The injured pilot, identified as Indian national Capt Smit Machchhar, was taken to hospital after the flight landed and later called a "hero" by the Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. 

Now, Israeli officials are investigating whether the stabbing was an act of terrorism – and whether any warning signs were missed.

author: BBC News
description:
Artificial intelligence (AI) could trigger financial market shocks and the UK needs to be prepared for them, the governor of the Bank of England has warned.

Andrew Bailey said the central bank is watching the huge amounts of money being invested in AI "very carefully" and cautioned that "not everybody always wins".

The money that has been spent on and loaned to AI firms over the last few years in the hope of large returns is causing markets to value some of them as multi-trillion dollar businesses.

author: BBC News
description:
Northern Ireland has introduced the UK's first ever graduated driving licences, bringing in the biggest change for new drivers in decades.  

The new rules will affect when you drive, how you drive and who you drive with. 

The measures are designed to reduce the number of young people killed or seriously injured on Northern Ireland's roads. 

Supporters argue the reforms will save lives and improve road safety. Young people argue that it limits their independence and won’t affect everyone equally. 

BBC Journalist Jake Wood travels across Northern Ireland to meet the people affected and asks whether graduated driving licences are the answer to making the roads safer. 

In this episode:

00:57 – What are graduated driving licenses? 
02:13 – Northern Ireland collision statistics  
02:55 – Jake speaks to the Infrastructure Minister, Liz Kimmins  
04:09 – Omagh: the effect on rural drivers  
06:30 – Back to Stormont: Liz
title: What will Northern Ireland's new driving rules mean for young motorists? | In Case You Missed It

Hundreds of prisoners across England and Wales are being released early today under a new scheme designed to free-up prison space. 

Offenders serving sentences of up to 19 months are now eligible for release after a third of their term.

Prisoners being released early today will include those convicted of fraud, domestic abuse and coercive control.

Restriction zones will control the movements of the most serious offenders, while the UK government promises a record roll-out of ankle monitors.

author: BBC News
description:
Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike has been taken to hospital after she was still alive following two lethal injections during her execution, her lawyer says.
 
Her legal team filed an emergency motion to halt the execution as it was happening, saying: "Ms Pike has lost consciousness and still has a heartbeat and is audibly snoring."
 
One of her attorneys told the BBC that Pike, 50, was "being provided life-saving measures" in hospital after two syringes of pentobarbital had been administered.
 
There has been no comment yet from the state of Tennessee. Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer.
